hints: Form tangent equation using gradient at $x = 6$.
walkthrough:
Find the $x$-intercept of the curve $y = 3 + 12(2 - x)^{-1}$ by setting $y = 0$:
$$3 + \frac{12}{2 - x} = 0 \implies \frac{12}{2 - x} = -3 \implies 2 - x = -4 \implies x = 6 \implies (6, 0)$$

Differentiate the curve equation with respect to $x$:
$$\frac{dy}{dx} = 12(-1)(2 - x)^{-2}(-1) = \frac{12}{(2 - x)^2}$$

Write the equation of the tangent line at $(6, 0)$:
$$y - 0 = \frac{3}{4}(x - 6) \implies y = \frac{3}{4}x - \frac{9}{2} \quad \left(\text{or } 3x - 4y = 18\right)$$

Evaluate the gradient of the curve at $x = 4$:
$$\left.\frac{dy}{dx}\right|_{x=4} = \frac{12}{(2 - 4)^2} = \frac{12}{4} = 3$$

Apply the chain rule for rates of change with $\frac{dx}{dt} = 0.04\text{ units s}^{-1}$:
$$\frac{dy}{dt} = \frac{dy}{dx} \times \frac{dx}{dt} = 3 \times 0.04 = 0.12\text{ units s}^{-1}$$
